D021-D017_h001.question:
I’ve always been mindful about my health, but over the past few months, it’s become harder to ignore the weight gain I’m terrified of. I’m not where I used to be—I don’t feel light on my feet anymore—and I’ve cut out bread, rice, anything starchy, just to feel in control. Sometimes I skip dinner if I feel like I ate too much earlier, though my husband worries. I tell him I’m fine, that I just “feel better” this way.

I check myself constantly in mirrors, store windows—anything reflective. My hands go to my waist without thinking, measuring. Even when people say I look thin, I don’t feel it. I just can’t trust how I look. At work, interpreting for clients all day, I’m so aware of my body in motion—my arms, my shape moving through space. I worry they’re watching not just my signs, but *me*. I’ve started wearing looser clothes to feel less exposed, even in the summer.

I don’t know if it’s about weight exactly, or just… not feeling right in my skin. But I can’t stop focusing on it. I don’t know if I’m protecting my health or punishing myself. And I don’t know what would happen if I just… ate.
D021-D017_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D021-D017_h001.answer: A & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

I know I’m lean—my uniform hangs a bit loose now—but the idea of gaining weight makes my chest tighten. My squad’s noticed. They tease me about skipping chow, but it’s not funny to me.

I can’t stop looking in mirrors, side views, reflections in windows. Not because I think I look bad—I don’t even know what I’m checking. Just… not right. But it’s not just size. Sometimes it’s my face, my posture, like something’s off but I can’t name it. I don’t know how long this has been going. A few months? Feels longer.

I don’t know if it’s about looks exactly. I just feel like if I let up, even a little, things will spin out of control. D021-D017_h004.question:

I prep meals at home myself, no one else touches them. I measure oils, avoid frying, skip the butter people expect in sauces. At work, I might taste, but I won’t eat a full plate. It’s not about health anymore. It’s like my body’s not mine unless I’m restricting. But I wouldn’t say I hate my face, or anything like that. It’s more… the weight. The idea of it. D021-D017_h021.question:
I’ve always been mindful about my diet, but over the past few months, I’ve started paying closer attention. I avoid carbs pretty much entirely—no bread, pasta, rice—and I don’t eat any added fats, like cooking oil or butter. It just feels safer that way. I can’t really explain it, but the idea of gaining weight freaks me out, even though I’m not heavy. My coworkers have mentioned I look thin, and I’ve noticed my hair thinning, and I get dizzy standing up too fast, but I figure that’s just stress or not sleeping well.

I spend a lot of time at my desk—it’s part of the job as a developer—so I’m not moving around much. I check my reflection often, especially when I’m walking past glass or my monitor screen. I guess I’m just… not comfortable with how I look, but it’s not like I can point to one thing. It’s more of a general feeling. I don’t take selfies anymore, and I avoid group photos. I wouldn’t say I’m obsessed, but it’s definitely on my mind a lot.

I don’t see a problem with my eating, though. I feel in control. Even if I’m tired or my clothes hang loose, it seems worth it to not let go of that control. I don’t know if any of this means I should be worried.
D021-D017_h021.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D017_h021.answer: C & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h022.question:
I’ve been trying to eat “clean” for about the past six months—nothing processed, very little sugar, and I cap my calories at around 800 a day. I work long hours at the hospital, so I tell myself I don’t need much fuel. I bring a small salad or a piece of fruit and call it lunch. High-calorie foods scare me—I know it sounds intense, but if I eat something like pasta or even an avocado, I feel like I’ll gain weight overnight.  

I know people say I look thin, but I don’t see it the same way. I just want to be healthy. My assistant recently asked if I’m okay, and my primary doctor brought up low iron and my weight last visit, but I don’t think it’s that serious. I feel fine—tired sometimes, but who isn’t? I’m in control.  

There are days I stand in front of the mirror longer than I should, checking… not sure what I’m looking for, really. Not just weight—I don’t know how to explain it. It’s like something’s off, but I can’t pinpoint it. I don’t have time for therapy. I just need to stay disciplined. I can manage this on my own.
D021-D017_h022.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D017_h022.answer: C & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h023.question:
I’ve been keeping a close eye on my weight for about a year now—maybe a little over. I step on the scale every morning, and sometimes a few times a day, just to make sure things haven’t shifted. Even a pound gain makes me pretty anxious. I work retail, so I’m on my feet all day, but I still worry I’m not doing enough.

I’ve cut out a lot of stuff from my diet—no bread, no pasta, and I avoid anything with visible fat. I don’t really feel hungry most of the time, or maybe I’ve just gotten used to ignoring it. My coworkers have mentioned I look thin, and my mom keeps asking if I’m eating enough, but I tell them I feel better this way—I’ve got more control.

They don’t get it, honestly. I know my numbers—my weight, my measurements—and I’m not where I want to be yet. I just feel like if I relax even a little, everything will change. 

I do pay attention to how I look—it’s hard not to, especially when you’re around people all day. But it’s not like I’m staring in mirrors all the time or anything. It’s just… I want to look right. And I’m not sure I ever do.
D021-D017_h023.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D017_h023.answer: C & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h024.question:
I’ve been trying really hard to stay in control, especially with how I look. As a nurse, I’m on my feet all day, but honestly, I don’t eat much—maybe just a small salad or some veggies, sometimes coffee if I’m busy. I track calories closely; anything over 800 a day makes me really anxious. I know people say I’m too thin, but I can’t afford to gain weight. It would feel like losing control, like I was giving in to something dangerous. 

I check myself in mirrors sometimes, more than I’d like—especially in the staff restroom between shifts. I don’t know, I just need to make sure I still look… okay. Not fat. My coworkers have said I look tired, or pale, and my period stopped a few months back, but I’m not sick. I feel fine—better than fine, actually. Strong. Disciplined.

I don’t really focus on my face or anything like that. It’s more about how clothes fit. But I wouldn’t say I’m obsessed. I just need to stay on top of things. I know my weight’s low, but I’m not fragile. I work full-time, I run—normal stuff. I think people worry too much.
D021-D017_h024.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D017_h024.answer: C & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—since I came back from my last voyage, actually. Things at home have been tense. My wife keeps telling me I’m too thin, that I don’t eat enough, but I feel fine. I just haven’t had much of an appetite lately. I skip breakfast—it’s never really been a priority, even at sea—and sometimes I’m not hungry by dinner. If I do eat, it’s light. Fish, salad, that kind of thing.  

I check my weight now and then. Old habit from when the company required fitness checks. But now, if the number goes up even half a kilo, I get this… tightness in my chest. Like I’m losing control. So I’ll walk extra the next day or avoid dinner.  

My doctor said I’m underweight, but I told him he’s overreacting. I’m 60, not 30—of course I weigh less than I used to. He mentioned seeing a specialist, but I don’t see the point. I look in the mirror and I just see *me*. Not too thin, not too anything.  

Sometimes I catch myself turning sideways, checking my reflection, but it’s not about looks. It’s more about… feeling right. In balance.  

My wife says I’m obsessed, but I know my body better than anyone.
D021-D017_h025.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D017_h025.answer: C & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder
